profile.reading:
Csquare IAD2-A stands at 22810 International Drive in Sterling, Loudoun County, Virginia, one of two buildings on the operator's IAD2 campus, which the company's own specification sheet addresses as 22810 to 22860 International Drive. Loudoun County holds the densest concentration of data centre capacity anywhere in the world, and this building is one of its smaller survivors from an earlier era of the business, a carrier dense interconnection building rather than a hyperscale hall.

The operator is Csquare, which traded as Centersquare until recently. Brookfield Infrastructure created it in April 2024 by combining Cyxtera, bought out of Chapter 11 for 775 million dollars in a transaction completed in January 2024, with Evoque, the data centre business AT and T divested to Brookfield in 2019. The company went public on NASDAQ in July 2026 at 21 dollars per share. Its Form S-1 lists this building individually as IAD2_A with 49,427 square feet of sellable space, 55.7 percent leased and owned rather than leased by Csquare as of 31 March 2026, inside a portfolio of 64 facilities across 21 markets carrying 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity.

The power figures need separating carefully, because this is a case where the wrong number travels. Csquare's public specification sheet gives 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, and all three are campus totals covering IAD2-A and IAD2-B together across 48,169 square feet of raised floor. The 35.8 megawatt figure is the electrical service available to the campus, and it is the number directories most often reprint as though it were capacity. It is not capacity. The 8.5 megawatt UPS figure is the closest published bound on protected IT load, and even that is a two building number rather than this building's. The 20 megawatts of generators is standby diesel, which is generation and not load. Csquare publishes no IT load for IAD2-A on its own, so none is recorded here. For scale, the sibling IAD1 campus at 45845 Nokes Boulevard carries 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS and 37.5 megawatts of generators across 141,621 square feet, and holds an ENERGY STAR certification that IAD2 does not. IAD2 lists nine service providers on a carrier neutral basis against thirteen at IAD1, and the two campuses are joined by dark fibre so that a customer in either can reach the other's carriers without paying to cross a third party exchange.

Loudoun County's own published record puts this building in proportion. As of 1 March 2026 the county counted roughly 233 existing data centre buildings totalling about 56.5 million square feet, an average of about 234,000 square feet each, with roughly 35.7 million square feet approved but not yet built and a further 21 applications covering about 56 buildings and 20.7 million square feet still in legislative review. Permits issued in 2025 alone exceeded 10 million square feet, the highest single year on record. The county attributes more than 17,000 direct and indirect jobs to the industry and reports 1.2 billion dollars of real and personal property tax revenue from data centres in fiscal year 2026, about 39 percent of its entire budget, projected to rise to 1.3 billion dollars and 40 percent in fiscal 2027. On 18 March 2025 the Board of Supervisors ended by right data centre development altogether, so a new project now requires a special exception with public hearings before the Planning Commission and the Board, with grandfathering only for applications already under review on 12 February 2025 and only where the site stands more than 500 feet from residential areas. IAD2-A long predates that shift, and at under 50,000 square feet of sellable space it is roughly a fifth the size of the average data centre building already standing in Loudoun and about a seventh of the average recently permitted one. That is the honest frame for this row. It is a small, well connected, majority leased interconnection asset sitting inside a county whose new supply is measured in an entirely different unit.

What is not established is the year IAD2-A was built, the identity of its electric utility, which Csquare does not name in any published material, and any per building split of the campus power, cooling or generator figures.

reading.body:
Centersquare IAD2-A is one of two buildings on the operator's IAD2 campus at 22810 International Drive in Sterling, Loudoun County, Virginia. It is a small interconnection facility, built before the county ended by-right data centre development in March 2025, and now one of roughly 233 existing data centre buildings in Loudoun totalling about 56.5 million square feet. The county holds the densest concentration of data centre capacity anywhere in the world, and this building ranks 26th by published megawatts among all mapped facilities in Virginia.

Csquare publishes no IT load for IAD2-A individually. The operator's specification sheet gives three figures for the IAD2 campus as a whole: 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity and 20 megawatts of generators, covering both IAD2-A and IAD2-B together across 48,169 square feet of raised floor. The 35.8 megawatt utility power figure is electrical service available to the campus and not IT capacity. The 8.5 megawatt UPS capacity is the closest published bound on protected IT load and is still a two-building total. The 20 megawatts of generators is standby diesel and is generation rather than load. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, a standalone 8.5 megawatt protected load would support roughly 212 racks, but that is a campus figure and this building's share is not published.

The building holds SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it to host compliance-sensitive workloads across multiple regulatory regimes. It connects by dark fibre to Csquare's larger IAD1 campus 5 miles away at 45845 Nokes Boulevard, which carries 143.2 megawatts of utility power and holds ENERGY STAR certification that IAD2 does not. At under 50,000 square feet of sellable space, IAD2-A is roughly one-fifth the size of the average existing data centre building in Loudoun and about one-seventh the size of buildings permitted since 2023, making it a legacy asset in a county now building at a much larger scale.
